text:
mike: Quick heads-up — ran a small mini-bench after the slab-rebalance change and seeing a 5-12% p95 regression on 8k seq workloads (A100). Not an across-the-board perf drop but tail is worse when KV cache is active. Repro steps and logs below.

mike: repro cmd:
```
./bench_runner --model gpt-neox-20b --seq_len 8192 --batch 2 --warmups 20 --iters 200 --kernels probe,choose
```
logs: chooser picked Triton-attn for most batches but then fell back to FlashAttention/cuBLASLt during 3 concurrent requests -> observed OOM-ish allocate failures and retries. Snippet: 
```
[chooser] picked triton_attn (est_workspace=1.2G)
[alloc] slab_alloc(1.2G) -> success
[exec] triton_attn start
[alloc] kv_cache_grow 256M -> slab_fragmentation=0.42
[exec] triton_attn kernel failed (cudaErrorMemoryAllocation) -> fallback to flashattn (est=980M)
[alloc] slab_alloc(980M) -> reserve_probe=true -> success
```

anya: Can you paste the perf trace / telemetry id? Curious whether the fragmentation spike aligns with a particular sequence length or batch size. Also which quant/precision and cudnn/cuBLAS versions?

mike: telemetry: https://telemetry.internal/runs/bench/1965554321 (flamegraphs + allocator traces). Using fp16, cuBLASLt 11.11, Triton kernels built from release-2025-02. Fragmentation ratio seems to jump when kv cache grows > ~40% of slab size.

sanjay: sounds like allocator headroom assumptions got tighter after rebalance. If the rebalance is consolidating hot slabs it might leave more small fragments elsewhere. Two quick ideas: 1) increase probe-reserve from 0.05 -> 0.12 for attn/ffn allocations when kv_in_use, 2) enable opportunistic compaction on low throughput (force-compact when util < 0.25).

taylor: +1 on opportunistic compaction. We should be careful — compaction can stall tail latency if done synchronously. Maybe do async compaction during idle gaps or piggyback on batch boundaries. Also consider tweaking kernel chooser to prefer FlashAttention for large seq lengths when slab_free_frag_ratio > 0.3 to avoid large single-block allocs.

mike: Agree — kernel chooser currently ranks by est_latency only. I'll add a frag-penalty term: score = latency + alpha * frag_penalty, where frag_penalty = max(0, slab_fragmentation_ratio - frag_threshold) * estimate_bytes. Quick local tweak (alpha=0.8, frag_threshold=0.25) reduced p95 by ~6% in the mini-bench.

anya: Nice. Can you commit the chooser patch as a temporary flag so we can A/B test? Also add metric slab_fragmentation_ratio to per-request telemetry (current metrics are too coarse).

mike: Yup, will make a PR: redwood/runtime#4721 (draft). It adds `--chooser-frag-alpha` and exposes `slab_fragmentation_ratio` and `kv_cache_bytes` per-request. Plan: land behind feature flag and run the nightly micro-bench suite.

sanjay: For OOM mitigation, also add a fast-path to try small realloc backoffs: if alloc(estimate) fails, try alloc(estimate * 0.75) with sticky-kv-evict hint; that avoids full fallback to a different kernel which can be more expensive. But we must ensure correctness (kernel workspace must meet minimum).

mike: Implemented a soft-backoff in the patch: try smaller workspace slices down to a min_workspace threshold, and if successful, mark the request as "reduced-workspace" in traces. In benches that avoided full fallback we see lower end-to-end p95 while keeping latency determinism.

taylor: Important: add a unit test that simulates kv growth + interleaved small allocations to reproduce fragmentation. We keep hitting flaky OOMs in CI without this.

infra-bot: Deployed mini-bench infra image `bench:a100-2026-03-18` to ci-runner-7 for running queued micro-bench slots.

mike: Next steps I propose:
- land chooser frag penalty behind flag (mike)
- add slab_fragmentation_ratio telemetry + dashboard (anya)
- add async compaction prototype + replay on low-util (sanjay)
- unit + micro-bench to reproduce frag path (taylor)

mike: assigning itself to PR cleanup and running nightlies. Will post results in this thread tomorrow with updated telemetry. Thanks for the quick feedback :thumbsup:
